newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani cotton rates rise on quality hunt.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani cotton rates rise on quality hunt.

text.p: Pakistani cotton rates rose on Sunday as spinners hunted good quality stocks and dealers said prices would rise further in the next few sessions.

"Spinners concerned about quality of fresh arrivals are paying higher to get better stuff," dealer Kishin Chand said. Estimates of lower output in the 1996/97 crop year had also prompted spinners to cover their future requirements.
In the kerb market, NIAB-78 variety was traded at 2,200 rupees ($54.69) per maund (37.32 kg), dealers said.
